metric_scope.metric: Estimated annual gross margin and associated debt-service calculation

inputs: Supplied model: principal P = USD 2,800 million
Supplied model: 12 interest-only months followed by 60 monthly amortizing payments
Supplied model: annual revenue R = USD 1,060 million
Supplied model: annual costs including depreciation, before financing C = USD 837.4 million
derived.formula: Monthly payment M = 2800*(0.06/12)/(1-(1+0.06/12)^(-60)) = 54.131844 million. Annual debt service = 12*M = 649.582131 million. First-year interest = 2800*0.06 = 168 million. First-year modeled percentage = (1060-837.4-168)/1060*100 = 5.150943%. Later modeled percentage = (1060-837.4-649.582131)/1060*100 = -40.281333%.
derived.rounding: Calculate without intermediate rounding; report payments to two decimal places in USD millions and percentages to two decimal places.

receipt.public_excerpt: Next, the cost of goods sold (COGS) is deducted from net sales in order to arrive at gross profit.

evidence_items.explanation: Applying the ordinary gross-profit definition to the same hypothetical inputs excludes loan payments. Even treating all $837.4 million of pre-financing costs as direct costs gives 21%, so financing does not turn this model's gross margin into approximately -40%.

metric_scope.metric: Estimated annual gross margin and associated debt-service calculation

inputs: Supplied model: annual revenue = USD 1,060 million
Supplied model: annual costs before financing, including depreciation = USD 837.4 million
Conservative classification for this check: all supplied pre-financing costs count as direct costs
derived.formula: Gross-margin check = (1060-837.4)/1060*100 = 21%. Loan interest and principal payments are excluded from this calculation.
derived.rounding: 21.00%; the exact classification of overhead could change the conventional gross margin, but cannot justify deducting loan principal.

unresolved_gaps: The commercial realism of the assumed revenue, utilization, costs, and financing terms has not been independently established.
The model does not separate all direct costs from overhead, preventing a precise conventional gross-margin calculation beyond the stated conservative check.
